classification.difficultyReason: Combine perpendicular constructions and compass transfer of equal lengths to construct a square.

content.prompt: Draw an interval then construct a square that has that interval as one of its sides.

answer.short: A square constructed on the chosen interval, with all four sides equal and all four angles right angles.
answer.worked:
Label the chosen interval $AB$. Using the straight-angle bisection construction, construct perpendicular rays to $AB$ at $A$ and $B$, on the same side of $AB$. Set the compasses to length $AB$. Mark $D$ on the perpendicular at $A$ so that $AD=AB$, and mark $C$ on the perpendicular at $B$ so that $BC=AB$. Join $C$ to $D$.

The equal perpendicular intervals $AD$ and $BC$ give $ABCD$ four right angles and $CD=AB$. Thus all four sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is a square.

spec.description: Authored sample square on an arbitrary interval AB. Dashed perpendicular extensions and equal-radius compass arcs indicate transfer of AB to AD and BC. No numerical side length is imposed.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DA; all interior angles are 90 degrees.
